utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Bajcetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, could I ask you to escort Mr. Bajcetic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bajcetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, Mr. Emmerson will continue his cross-examination, but I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony still binds you. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, I wonder if you could take -- or be given, first of all, the green and brown folders -- sorry, the yellow and brown folders, I apologise, the yellow being volume 1. If you can take volume 1, the yellow folder again, and turn to tab 14, which is your witness statement in these proceedings and I was asking you some questions when we broke last Thursday about paragraphs 42 through to 47.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just before we broke on Thursday, I asked you some questions about whether the information that is recorded in paragraphs 42 to 47 was first provided to you when the RDB operatives who had been present on the 8th returned to your offices. And you said at the very end of your cross-examination on Thursday that it was correct that you had not been provided during the day with any information by telephone or radio and that the first you learnt about it and what had been found that day was when they returned that evening. And you explained that there was no coverage for mobile phones in the area of the canal and that radio links were difficult as well because there were problems with transmission. Now, first of all, I just want to give you an opportunity to reflect on that answer. That is the correct position, is it, that you received no information by telephone or radio during the day on the 8th and that the first information you received was received in person when those operatives returned that evening?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard evidence in this court that by 4.00 that afternoon members of the international community had been summoned to the scene and that while Mr. Tomas was there that day and before he returned to your office, he saw Zoran Andjelkovic, president of the Kosovo Provisional Executive Council and Nikola Sainovic, deputy prime minister of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia attending the scene, as well as members of the media. I want to ask you: Given that there were no telephone or radio transmissions capable of being emitted from the scene, as far as you understood the position, can you help us as to how those individuals might have been notified of the find if it was genuinely found on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know how it came about that they were notified about it. That --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the last part of your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know how the people were informed because I wasn't there at the time nor was I informed of the way they received information about it. This was, indeed, found there because that was the information I received, that they had found dead bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, it appears inevitable from the evidence you've given, does it not, that not only were the press and the international community and the politicians informed before you were but that they attended the scene before you were even informed of what had been found?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who informed them. I cannot really comment on that. I am not familiar with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you turn to paragraph 71 of your witness statement, please. In paragraph 71, you are recorded as saying that: "On the 8th and the 9th of September, the RDB officers who were deployed on the spot reported to me, being their superior, their findings and I informed the Head of RDB Department in Gjakove, Mr. Sreten Camovic in line with the standard procedure." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that a correct statement of the position, Mr. Bajcetic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the standard procedure. On the 8th and the 9th, the operatives informed me about it, reported to me about it. Sreten Camovic even went over there at one point, but I wasn't with him there nor was there any need for him to inform me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is just what I wanted to clarify with you. Did Mr. Camovic go to the canal with the reconnaissance mission on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the time that elapsed, I really don't know. I'm sure that he was with me on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. You went there for the first time on the 10th and you've said in your witness statement that Mr. Camovic went with you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the question that I'm asking you is: In this paragraph of your witness statement, you appear to be indicating that on the 8th you received information from those who had been present and you conveyed that information to Mr. Camovic. What I'm trying to understand is, plainly, if Mr. Camovic was there on the 8th it would not have been necessary for you to have been the conduit for information that had been provided by RDB officers on the spot, would it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. The operatives who reported to me on what they had seen on the spot -- well, it was quite customary for Camovic and I to get together and to exchange views on what we just learnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I entirely understand that. But the question I'm asking you is whether Mr. Camovic went to the canal on the 8th with the reconnaissance mission, because clearly if he did, it wouldn't have been you reporting to him what the operatives had seen but him telling you what he had seen, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to the latter part of that question. It appears that Mr. Emmerson's drawing his own conclusion as opposed to formulating in the context of a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't really understand the objection. The question I'm asking is: Did Mr. Camovic go to the canal on the 8th? And the reason I'm asking the question as I explained is because if he had done, paragraph 71 does not appear to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Issa, isn't it true that putting a possible conclusion to a witness, if it is of a factual character, that that is within the scope of leading questions put to the witness, whereas if it would require a kind of expert opinion, then that would be different?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps it would make it easier if Mr. Emmerson breaks up the questions and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Having refreshed your memory from your witness statement, can you help us, was Mr. Camovic present at the reconnaissance mission on the 8th along with Bogdan Tomas and Mr. Jovovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Truly, I don't know. I can't remember the detail --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- those were very hard times. I don't want to go into that and describe how it was, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you're not able to remember, you're not able to remember. But can you help us about this: Does it follow from that that where you say in paragraph 71 that you were reporting the findings of the RDB operatives in the field on the 8th to Mr. Camovic, you may be wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I don't believe that follows if the witness indicated that he doesn't know if Camovic went to -- with the reconnaissance unit on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then he may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get matters straight. Mr. Bajcetic, Mr. Emmerson is wondering whether there was any need to report to Mr. Camovic what you have heard if he may have been present there. I think, Mr. Emmerson, that's your concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you help Mr. Emmerson in better understanding the situation because if Mr. Camovic was present there might have been no need to report to him. Does that mean that since you said you reported that it's more likely that he was not present? Or could it be that you made a mistake that due to his presence you didn't report to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was very clear in answering the question concerning paragraph 71. This was in the evening when the operatives reported to me on what they had seen at the spot and what had transpired during the day. They informed me of the fire they came under and the corpses at Radonjic Lake. I can't recall whether Camovic was there at the time or not. What is quite certain is that every evening Camovic and I exchanged views on the intelligence, on the information we received in the course of that day. I do not wish to improvise or speculate by trying to say for a fact that he was there or not. It is possible that he was, I even believe that he may have been, but I can't be sure. It was nine years ago, after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. I think, as a matter of fact, what Mr. Emmerson would expect that if he would have been present and if, as you say in paragraph 71 of your statement, that you informed Mr. Camovic in line with the standard procedure, Mr. Emmerson would expect him to say: Why do you inform me? I was there. Do you understand what I mean? That's the question that's bothering Mr. Emmerson. Can you help him out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regardless of whether he had been there or not, we always discussed such matters that were horrific in the course of the evenings. We would kind of go through all the information we got during the day in the evenings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you return then to paragraphs 44 to 47 of your witness statement, and I just want to pick up one aspect of that account with you, if I can. In paragraphs 44 to 46, you record an account that you say was given to you by the cameraman, Mr. Tomas, and Mr. Jovovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were they all together when they gave you this account?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who could remember such a detail nine years later? I believe I spoke to the cameraman first.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who was it, can you help us at all, who told you that there had been heavy shelling which caused the group of MUP and RDB officials to be detained for a couple of hours, awaiting the arrival of VJ reinforcements whilst they were en route to the canal? Where did that information come from?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that by the cameraman. He was quite disappointed with the fact that the support arrived quite late. I clearly recall that he wore leather sandals, that went to pieces, and he was barefoot as he entered the offices. He was pretty nervous and told me the whole story then. That's the information you're referring to. I don't know what else I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the information he gave you was that there was a two-hour exchange of fire prior to the arrival of VJ reinforcements, was it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you what he had told me, that mortar fire was opened, just as it is stated here. I can't remember his exact words now, nine years later. It's impossible, not just for me but for anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Help me, if you can, you signed this statement in May of this year, in which paragraph 45 you record and sign an account which states that there was an exchange of fire between the MUP and the KLA whilst the group were waiting for reinforcements, that the MUP returned fire from -- in the direction of the village of Ratis from where the convoy was being shelled, and that this situation lasted for a couple of hours until the MUP and VJ reinforcements arrived. That's the statement you referred to as having come from the cameraman, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you check that with the other two who were present, Mr. Tomas and Mr. Jovovic, to see if they agreed with it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information referred to here was quite immaterial, how many minutes or hours the shelling lasted; the important matter was that the men returned alive and well and the important bit of information was that corpses had been found at that scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just help us on one other aspect of this reconnaissance mission. Could you turn to tab 13, please, in the yellow file and just look at the front page and confirm that you know the individual who made that statement without mentioning his name, please?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have described him in your own witness statement by reference to his responsibilities at paragraph 57. I won't read it out, but perhaps you can confirm that the description you've given in paragraph 57, in the second half of paragraph 57 of your own witness statement is correct.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is an individual who was closely involved with this investigation in a supervisory capacity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we then turn to tab 13 again, his witness statement, and that paragraph 13 where he lists those who took place -- who took part, I'm sorry, in the reconnaissance mission. And if you pick it up halfway down the paragraph, paragraph 13, he refers to, first of all, the SUP team who made the first crime scene visit at the canal. And he lists the following persons: General-Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic, chief of public security sector for the MUP Serbia; Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic, deputy chief of security; chief of Gjakove SUP, Dragutin Adamovic; chief of Gjakove state security, Sreten Camovic; crime inspector Goran Mitic; crime inspector Dusan Dragovic; crime technician Nebojsa Avramovic; crime technician Zarko Gazdic; and from the state security sector he says the following members formed part of this team, late crime inspector Dejan Jovovic and crime technician Sava Jovanovic, who was in charge of -- for video-recording. And he goes on to say before they reached the actual crime site they didn't know exactly the location of the killed persons. Now, pausing there for a moment, we can see that this witness does not mention Mr. Tomas amongst those who attended. Are you clear in your own mind that Mr. Tomas was amongst those who attended the canal on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With that exception, do you have any reason to doubt the accuracy of the list that he has set out in that witness statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that the list that is set out in the witness statement -- I'll just repeat what I was about to say. You mentioned a moment ago that the list of names set out in the witness statement behind tab 13 concerns individuals from the public security sector rather than the state security sector. And obviously we can see that the name of Mr. Camovic, Mr. Jovovic, and Mr. Jovanovic are all there. They, of course, were state security employees; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it your evidence in effect that you don't know the identity of those members of the MUP or SUP who attended on the 8th, but you do know the identity of those members of the RDB who attended?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the persons from the public security are concerned, I do know some of them. As for the state security staff, I know all of them, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, can I simply ask you this: Would you agree that that is a very high-ranking group of individuals to attend a crime scene, the location of which was unknown and where it was perceived that there was a risk of a reconnaissance mission coming under fire, would you agree that it's a very high-ranking group of individuals to attend on such a reconnaissance mission?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand why you're asking me this. I was not in a position to determine who would be there on that day. I did not have anything to say about that day, who was going to be there. I wasn't there. That's the only thing I can tell you. And I have told you clearly what was conveyed to me on that evening. As for the other facts, it's very hard to remember things after nine years. As for the level and the rank of the people in the mission and what they were supposed to be, I'm really not in a position to tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Let me take it down to your own level then specifically. Does it strike you, looking back on those events, as surprising that your superior, Mr. Camovic, would attend on a reconnaissance mission if the site and the location was unknown?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why this should have surprised me. Camovic could do whatever he wanted. He was my superior and he did not have to inform me where he was going and who with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could try to -- you have -- until now, you have expressed, Mr. Bajcetic, two times your surprise -- being surprised why these questions are put to you. What Mr. Emmerson is trying to find out, whether on such a reconnaissance mission where you do not know yet what to find, et cetera, why - may I say it - quite some big-shots participated in that and whether that would be what one would expect, in view of what would be the usual procedure. I think that's what Mr. Emmerson would like to know, not whether you were in a position to criticise or to decide how the mission was, but whether it surprised you that very high-level authorities participated in such a visit to what might be a crime scene where little was known at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can share my views with you. At that time I didn't know who would be going on that mission, and as I sit here today I can tell you that this was a rather unusual situation for such high-ranking officials to go there to that site. This was not a customary thing. This was not something that was normally done. This is the only thing I can tell you today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What made the situation unusual, because I do understand that that explains for you why the high-level authorities went there. Looking back, do you know what made it so unusual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What made the situation unusual was the fact that there was a lot of information about the number of missing, about the great number of people missing. There were reasonable grounds to suspect that they were no longer among the living, and the KLA were supposed to have kidnapped them and killed them. This is what I've already told you, and I'm repeating it again. This is why everything was focused on trying to find these people. Now, as to the level of the mission and why those particular people went on that mission, I really wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I then understand you well that you say that expectations were high that perhaps a clue could be found for many unresolved disappearances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, to paragraphs 85 to 87 of your witness statement. I'm just going to go through those with you briefly, if I can. You are commenting in this part of your witness statement on the video footage that you have reviewed, which is said to have been taken on the 8th of September during the course of the afternoon, and you say: "With respect to the recordings made of the site at the canal and the canyon, it has to be stressed that the two bodies, which can be seen on the video footage, recorded on the 8th September 1998, cannot be seen anymore on the video footage made on the 9th and 10th of September, 1998. One of the bodies is wearing a red shirt and the second one is wearing a blue one. "The reason why those two bodies cannot be seen anymore on these dates because heavy rain on the 8th of September caused the water to sweep both bodies downstream towards the take. I know this based on what the cameraman told me and because the recording was different than what we saw on the 10th of September. The cameraman told me the bodies were present on the 8th but they were not present on the 10th of September." And then you say: "I saw these two bodies on the 10th of September downstream in the direction of the lake at approximately 200 metres from the location at the concrete canal, where they were initially seen on the 8th of September, 1998. I saw them in the pit between the earth and the natural bed on the 10th of September, 1998. The difference in the water-level on the 9th and the 10th of September can be noticed on the video" -- I'm sorry, "on the recordings made on those days." Now, pausing there for a moment to let the translation catch up. You are referring in that passage to two fully-fleshed bodies that can be seen in the video footage floating in the concrete section of the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you're commenting on the fact that they do not appear in the video footage for the following day, the 9th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the concrete part.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Or, indeed, on the video anywhere else, I think.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've limited myself to the concrete section.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you can confirm certainly that by the time you first got there on the 10th, they were not in the concrete section of the canal. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you say that you saw them, those two bodies, 200 metres downstream. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you, yourself, go down to the canyon section to look at those two bodies on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, my task was not to look at every body separately. First of all, I saw all the bodies that were on the side towards the concrete section, and I also saw the bodies that were under the cascade that went down the canyon towards Lake Radonjic. My task, therefore, was not to approach every body, to inspect every body, but I saw all of them from there, the bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just concentrate, please, if you can, Mr. Bajcetic, on my question. I understand the explanation that you've given that it wasn't your task to examine the bodies individually, but you have included in your witness statement an assertion that the two bodies that can be seen in the concrete section of the canal on the 8th were seen by you on the 10th 200 metres down from the concrete section along the canyon. And I'm trying to understand how you were in a position to say that the remains that you saw 200 metres down in the canyon were the same as the remains that can be seen on the video on the 8th. So my question is: Did you, yourself, go down into the canyon section on the 10th or were you viewing it from an elevated position?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If these two bodies had been in the concrete section above the cascade -- actually, the cameraman was what -- who told me that. He marked these two bodies. One was described as having a red shirt and the other blue shirt, and he told me that they were in the canyon. One could see that also from the elevation because there was some gravels there, I suppose to bury the bodies, the bodies that were on the bank. And from that position, one could see the two bodies as well as the other bodies, and the car where the bodies of two Albanians were, the husband and the wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, the last question was very simple, whether you went down into the canyon, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have immediately said: No, I didn't go down, then Mr. Emmerson will have follow-up questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me see if I can just unpick the last answer that you've given. Clearly - and we can all see this from the video - those two bodies were no longer in the concrete section of the canal in the piece of footage that was shown on the 9th; that much we can all agree upon. What I'm interested in is: Why it is you make a positive assertion in your witness statement that they were, those two particular bodies, were to be seen 200 metres downstream in the canyon when you arrived on the 10th. Now, is it the position that this is something you were told by the cameraman, or is this a position that you are giving evidence on oath that you saw those bodies there, 200 metres down in the canyon, and could identify them yourself as being the same bodies as were shown in the video of the 8th, floating in the concrete section of the canal, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, in your question you are creating two possibilities. The witness said already that he was told this. So in addition to what he was told and not -- it's not an or question, one or the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please make the question clear in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, were you told by the cameraman or by anybody else that the two bodies that had been seen on the 8th could be seen 200 metres down in the canyon on the 10th? Is that something you were told, first of all?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The cameraman told me that and I've already explained what he had told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you, yourself, see those two bodies or were you relying on what the cameraman said?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you what the cameraman told me. These two bodies could clearly be seen on the footage that he recorded on the 10th when we were together. You can see that clearly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in his photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think there may be some dispute about that, in terms of that in terms of what the video footage shows. The question I'm asking you, and I'll just put it simply to you again: Did you, yourself, personally look at those two bodies and identify them as being the same as the two bodies that you could see in the video footage of the 8th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The video footage that was recorded on the 10th when I was with the cameraman, those are the authentic images of what could be seen in the canyon -- of the canal, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you happen to make a note anywhere of the passage on the video where you say those two bodies can be seen, 200 metres down?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was watching the footage, I saw the two bodies, and I claim that I was at the lake on the 10th with the cameraman; and I claim that the footage that was made on the 10th are authentic and I have no reason to doubt that what he recorded on the 9th or on the 8th are not authentic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My question is: Did you make a note or a record of the time-counter on the video, which you say shows those bodies 200 metres down in the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was not duty-bound to record the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the cameraman who did that and I've already told you he was not a person who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, Mr. Emmerson just wants to know whether you made any note, not whether you had to do it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or it was someone else who should have done that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer seems simply to be no. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, by the time you were there on the 10th, the flow of water into the canal and the canyon had been very substantially reduced by manipulation of the gates further up the canal, had it not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cameraman told me that the level of the water was high and that there was a risk that all the bodies in the canal at the moment would be taken to the lake. I don't know about manipulated, I don't know that expression. What I know is the canal was closed in Donja Luka or Gornja Luka village where that was possible, and then the level of the water was reduced and that's why the corpses could not be carried all the way down to the lake. That's the essence of the whole matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that happened on the 9th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when this was closed. In any case, on the 10th the level of the water there was not that high, it was rather low.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. If you look at paragraph 88 of your witness statement, first sentence, you say it happened on the 9th; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so by the 10th, the level of water was low and not sufficient to carry bodies along the canyon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the gates were closed, that was no longer possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, if I tell you, Mr. Bajcetic, that no remains were recovered 200 metres down in the canal at the location you describe at all, would that affect your evidence or your recollection of this matter, that there were no remains recovered 200 metres down the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only influence can be the distance, 200 metres or any other distance. From the concrete part down the stream, I don't know how far it was, but on the -- in the footage that was recorded on the 10th of September you can see that there were corpses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll obviously review the footage. You're not able to help us as to the passage you're trying to rely on? When you viewed it with the Prosecution you made no note of the passage you're referring to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what footage you are referring to. I don't know what I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to the footage that you are seeking to suggest shows these two sets of remains 200 metres down in the canal, and I'm asking you to confirm that when you viewed this video footage with the Prosecution you made no note of the passage that you are identifying as showing those two sets of remains in the canyon?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It's very difficult for me to say whether this is the case or not from this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Would you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- did you understand the question put to you by Mr. Emmerson? Mr. Emmerson said you're relying on what you saw on the video but you did not make any note which portion exactly you were viewing when you gave this part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to tab 16, please, in the bundle, the yellow bundle. This contains Serbian and English translations of the reports of the diving team that attended the canal investigation, and if you would like to look, please, at the first document which is 16A, I'm going to direct your attention to paragraphs 1 and 3. Paragraph 1 records that: "On the 12th of September, between 1630 and 1345 hours," there must be some error in that record, "a diving team from the 'Belgrade' pier border police station from Belgrade," then the names are given, "searched the field and discovered the following." And then in the third paragraph, it reads as follows: "It was observed that the mud current does not allow for the hypothesis that the main stream of the canal water could have carried any object, such as the body of a person who drowned or another body, into the deeper part of the lake. This would indicate that the mud is an obstacle to bodies being carried into the depth of the lake." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if you turn to 16C there's a further report from the team of divers dated the 16th of September. And if you look to the fourth full paragraph on the first page, it refers back to those findings on the 12th. "On this day, the team concluded there was no possibility of bodies being carried into lake -- into Radonjic lake by the canal's main current. Even with high water-levels, the mud barriers would have retained any bodies from the canal. In this particular case, the quantity of water was small and the lake level was significantly lower than usual." A little further down, it says: "On the 13th and 14th September, following heavy rainfall, the water-level in the canal on and below the concrete areas had grown considerably. The water mass increased seven- to eight-fold and the flooding prevented any type of search of the canal." Then the penultimate paragraph of this report reads as following: "The team concluded that all the bodies found and any bodies that had made their way to the canal bed, whether the concrete or non-concrete part, under any type of circumstance could not have been carried into the lake regardless of the strength of the water current. There are several obstacles in the canal such as bushes, wedged branches, rocks, and sandbanks, especially where it winds around, which could retain bodies. Consequently, the uncemented section of the canal was searched in detail." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you are correct, Mr. Bajcetic, that the two bodies that are seen on the 8th in the concrete section of the canal were washed over into the canyon, then would you agree that they ought to have been recovered by the Serbian recovery operation that you observed and should be recorded on the post mortem examinations that were conducted at Hotel Pashtrik?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: First of all, the witness has no way of knowing that; secondly, that's assuming that those bodies had not, in fact, been recovered. We don't actually know that at this point. And I think the passages that Mr. Emmerson read from refer specifically to the lake, to the water current, pushing bodies into the lake itself, as opposed to the natural part of the canal, which is a distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are here really asking for conclusions, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll put the question another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please put the question another way. I tend to support Ms. Issa's reference to the passages you read.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you pause, please, before answering the next question to see if there is an objection. Based upon what you observed during your visit to the canal, and in particular what you say you saw in relation to these two bodies, can you provide the Trial Chamber with any explanation as to how those two bodies do not feature in any of the post mortem reports?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to have a factual foundation for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- order in which the evidence is called. The evidence of the forensic pathologist is to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Of course the Chamber doesn't know that either at this moment, but one way or the other this assumption should be clarified to the witness, either through a hypothetical assumption, to say if these bodies would not be, would have an explanation for that. That's a question -- and then of course Ms. Issa knows better what, on the basis of disclosures, is still to be expected as evidence, and if she would then strongly object, I would then suggest that we have a bit of an earlier break and that you explain to Ms. Issa what you're relying on and it's not just assumptions without any proper basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy to put the question in that form, if that is not going to be the subject of objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, would that be acceptable for you or would you still object? Because in that case --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't -- perhaps the witness might take his ear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps the witness takes his earphones off. Ms. Issa, it seems that Mr. Emmerson takes the view that these bodies are not part of the reported bodies at Hotel Pastrik, I think, and you seem to take a different position. Of course the -- Mr. Emmerson is entitled to ask a possible explanation to this witness, who, well, was participating in the investigations. If, however, you would have very strong feelings as that these two bodies were covered by the post mortem exercise at a later stage, then of course perhaps it would be good that you inform Mr. Emmerson on where you find those two bodies in the records.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's not a question of -- that those two bodies were, in fact, part of the post mortem record; it's a question of whether or not Mr. Emmerson is correct by suggesting that the bodies were simply not there. We don't know that. There are a number of bodies that were found in the natural part of the canyon by the forensic experts, which Your Honours will hear about shortly. But we simply don't know that, so Mr. Emmerson is actually assuming facts that are not in evidence when he -- when he puts his question in that way. We do not know if those two bodies formed part of the several bodies that were, in fact, found in the natural part of the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour. I know that Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- is more than capable of taking care of his own presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the nevertheless you would like to assist him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would like the make the following comment. I think Ms. Issa has, in a fundamental sense, avoided the Chamber's question, and that's the real problem, that if Mr. Emmerson poses the question in one fashion, it gives rise to an objection which is that it calls for speculation. If he poses the question the Chamber has suggested as to hypothetical, based upon evidence that we have received from the Prosecution and Ms. Issa decides to object to the question on that basis then we are in the exact position that you have suggested, where we need to have a discussion between counsel to make a determination of the precise evidence, because we are talking about two fully-fleshed bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I do understand, Ms. Issa, is that you do not disagree with Mr. Emmerson; that, as you said -- they were not identified as such in the post mortem records. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: They were not identified as those specific bodies that were in the concrete canyon on the 8th; however, there are a number of bodies that were found in the natural part of the canyon that -- which could be any number -- it could be any one of those bodies. So my objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact, it could not be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but my objection is that by suggesting to the witness that the bodies simply were not there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- that's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do it in a different way. Mr. Emmerson, if you would ask the witness perhaps on the basis that you were not able to find these two bodies among those who were covered by the post mortem and whether the witness has any explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then perhaps of course one of the next questions could be whether there would be a possibility that the witness -- that the bodies never had been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't want there to be any misunderstanding about my position. If the Prosecution is able to identify from the finite number of post mortem examination reports that are in their possession one or two which they suggest are capable of relating to the two floating bodies on the 8th then we would respectfully invite them to indicate which they are. This is not the first time I've raised this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I wouldn't have made the submissions that I have made, or asked the questions that I have made unless I had without a basis for doing it. And if there is a basis to contradict what I'm suggesting, then we would respectfully invite the Prosecution to identify it, certainly before the forensic pathologists are called, which are the bodies that they saw could be the two bodies seen in the video on the 8th floating in the concrete section of the canal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Issa, I've got one other question for you in this respect that isn't it true under Rule 90(H), that Mr. Emmerson even has a duty to put to the witness what their case is, and then of course put questions in relation to that. And the case apparently is that these bodies were not there at the time. So therefore, I think Mr. Emmerson is -- even has a duty to put that to the witness before he asks further questions about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's true that he does have a duty to put his case to the witness; the difficulty is he doesn't have a foundation, in my respectful submission, to put it in those terms, that the bodies simply were not there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that's his case he has to put it to the witness; whether he has good reasons to do so or not, we'll find out if it comes to the point of the presentation of the Defence case. But you can't say you are not allowed because you have got no good reasons for that. We are not yet at the stage where we can assess that properly. Perhaps you may have the impression you can. The Chamber certainly has not, and the Chamber has to supervise the proceedings, so Mr. Emmerson has a duty and it will later turn out whether he had a good reason or not to take that position. So to that extent, perhaps not hidden somewhere in the questions but more explicitly Mr. Emmerson puts to the witness what the Defence thinks the case is and then ask questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I do understand Your Honour's point, but my objection was -- the basis of my objection is that through, his question, Mr. Emmerson is assuming facts that are not in evidence and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he has no foundation for his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would that's part of the definition of a leading question. Leading questions are allowed in cross-examination, that is, either you already suggest an answer to the witness, or that the question includes assumptions on matters that are not yet proven. I mean, that's exactly -- I think, that's at least how I learned, what a leading question is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I agree with Your Honour that that's -- he's permitted to ask leading questions. My point is he's suggesting to the witness that the bodies simply were not there on the basis of not -- of the post mortem reports, and I'm -- my objection is that that's -- that's -- that would be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps -- perhaps, Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you would just put it to the witness and I tend to agree with Ms. Issa that you could not come to that conclusion on the basis of the post mortem records because in the post mortem records there seem to be quite a number of unidentified witnesses -- bodies, nevertheless, you think that they teach you more.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the post mortem report records what has been recovered. The age and state of decomposition of the remains, those parts of the bodies that have been recovered and they are photographed both in situ and during the PM -- post mortem procedure itself. And it's on the basis of that and with the benefit of expert opinion that I put the question that I do. I don't with to continue, to use up valuable cross-examination time debating an issue which is, for this witness, one which is put on an assumptive basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at the same time you were wise enough not to elicit any expert analysis by this witness of the post mortem records. So let's leave it out for a second and you can put your case to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and ask questions about it. Could you please put your earphones on again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, first of all, if you assume for a moment - the question I'm about to ask you proceeds on an assumption - assuming that there is no post mortem report which relates to any set of remains that could be either of those two floating bodies that are seen in the videotape on the 8th, is there anything which you saw which might account for that during the times that you were at the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that you're mentioning the canal, you quoted sections of some other reports. There are two sites involved. One is 200 metres off the cascade, of the concrete section toward Lake Radonjic; and the other one is 300 metres removed from the lake toward the canal, where there's also sludge. On the other side, there is no sludge, so there is a difference there as well. Now, as for this other issue you're mentioning, I don't really get the point of your question. The corpses were up at the cascade and then they were down there in the canal. This is something you can see in the footage. I don't see what else I can say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question I'm asking you, Mr. Bajcetic, is: Assume for a moment that there are no records showing that those two bodies were recovered and taken to Hotel Pashtrik and examined - in other words, that none of the post mortem reports on the remains that were allegedly recovered could be either of these two bodies, assume that is the position - was there anything that you saw or which you know about which could explain how two bodies in the canal could go missing?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to turn, please, to the brown file for a moment behind tab 1. This is a record made by the investigating judge - and I won't mention his name - on the 17th of September, confirming the dates on which the forensic team from Belgrade, led by Professor Dunjic, were present at the scene and at Hotel Pashtrik. You with see that the first date is the 11th of September and the last date is the 17th of September. I'd like you to confirm, please, that the forensic team arrived on the 11th, that is to say the day after you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any contacts with the forensics team. I only knew that they were operating in Hotel Pastrik.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, there was a forensic team at the canal, was there not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. I was not together with the forensic team. I did not have any contacts with them either when they were at the canal or when they were on the hotel premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Let me just be clear. You were at the canal on both the 10th and the 11th; is that correct, Mr. Bajcetic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was at the canal on the 10th. I was in Dasinovac on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So you never went to the canal on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Certainly there was no forensic team at the canal when you were there on the 10th, was there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there was. Something was being done there. There was a truck holding communications equipment or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, that - and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong - that the evidence is undisputed that Professor Dunjic and Professor Aleksandric first arrived on the 11th. And I wanted in that context to ask you to one matter of detail, if I could. Could you turn to volume 2, tab 2, the following tab. Yes. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could the volume be put a bit higher. Higher, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you hear me well now?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to volume 2, tab 2, and behind letter B, first of all, you'll find a photo -- two photographs. Although they're black and white, can I ask you, please, if you look at the bottom photograph you can see a still photograph of those two sets of fully-fleshed remains adjacent to the wall of the canal. Do you see in the bottom photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And those are the ones that you're referring to in the videotape of the 8th, are they not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And of one thing, or two things, we can be categorically certain on your evidence. The first is that those two sets of remains had gone by the 9th, is that correct, because they are not on the video footage for the 9th in that position.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't there on the 10th when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just take it in stages, please. On the evidence you have given we can be certain from what you yourself have told us that those two bodies which were there on the video on the 8th had gone from the concrete section of the canal by the 9th, because you've told us that you viewed that video and they had gone from that location by the 9th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was quite clear. In the video showed to me by the cameraman, I saw the two corpses and I do state for a fact that they weren't there on the 10th when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So -- again, I'm just going from your witness statement. You say in -- in paragraph 85 that those two bodies are not on the footage in that location on the 9th or the 10th and that the reason for that is that they are said to have been washed over by heavy rains on the night of the 8th; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I said is true. On the 8th there were corpses to be seen in the footage. On the 10th, they were no longer there because they had been washed over by the water, and in order to prevent other corpses from being washed over, the canal was closed. I believe we explained all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You -- just listen, if you can, carefully to my question. Paragraph 85 of your witness statement, which I read to you a little while ago and which you looked at, says that -- as far as those two bodies are concerned says this: "... The two bodies which can be seen on the video footage, recorded on the 8th of September, cannot be seen anymore on the video footage made on the 9th and the 10th September." And you say a little further on that the cameraman told you that they were present on the 8th but that they were not present on the 10th. Now just so that we're clear, you made a clear statement in your witness statement that the two bodies we can see in the video footage for the 8th by the wall in the concrete section of the canal, are no longer to be seen in the video footage for the 9th - never mind the 10th, but for the 9th. Is that correct, what you say in your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me think it over a bit. On the 8th the corpses were present. On the 9th - and I'm presuming on the basis of what the cameraman said - that on the 9th, the dam at Gornja Luka village was closed and that the corpses flowed on on the 9th and were not -- and could not be seen on the 10th. It's difficult to say now what exactly happened on the 8th and on the 9th and on the 10th, but I can tell you for a fact is on the 8th the corpses were there, on the basis of what the cameraman told me, and that they were no longer there on the 10th when I was there, and that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, let's use the 10th as our -- as our focus then rather than the 9th, because you're certain from your own observations that they were not there on the 10th; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now would you just turn in tab 2 to letter A, which refers to that photograph that I've just shown you. This is an extract from a transcript of the evidence given by the pathologist Professor Dunjic in the Milutinovic trial just immediately behind --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, the witness has it, in fact. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of the first page, line 122, Professor Dunjic is asked by reference to that paragraph which is 6D97 and he's asked: "Professor Dunjic, we should shortly see on the screen photographs that we procured from a book, and they should relate to the time when you were in that location. Is that the canal that we see on the screen? "A. Yes" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Yes, that's the canal. Those two photographs were taken from the direction of Radonjic Lake, and the place where the canal narrows down faces Donji Radiste and Glodjane. That's the concrete part of the canal. And the second photograph is something that I saw with my own eyes when I was on the location. We see two bodies next to the right-hand edge, depending on where you're looking from, two bodies that were floating and that were later found in the earth-covered part of the canal, because this is the concrete part. Out of the concrete part there is a waterfall and then follows an earthen part. There were heavy rainfalls at the time and these two bodies and a larger one were found in April." Now, pause there for a moment, if you will. If it's right - and I believe it is uncontested - that Professor Dunjic first arrived at the canal on the 11th of September, then on your testimony he cannot have seen those two bodies in the location where they appear in the photograph that you have just looked at, can he, because they had gone by then. Is that right? Pardon? I can't hear your answer, I'm sorry, is that correct --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- I -- before you -- before the witness answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The passage -- perhaps he should take his headphones off, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your headphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: There's a real lack of clarity, in my respectful submission, in terms of what this passage refers to because if we see the bottom part from where Mr. Emmerson just read from it says that the two bodies were floating and they were found in the earth-covered part of the canal because it was a concrete part. Then it continues on and talks about the heavy rainfalls at the time. So I'm not entirely sure without looking at the full context of the transcript and see what was said later on is whether or not Professor Dunjic referred to what he saw on that day or whether or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not at this moment, Ms. Issa, we are not judging the truthfulness of the testimony of Dr. Dunjic. "The second photograph is something I saw with my own eyes when I was at the location." There could hardly be any doubt as to that portion of his evidence. I mean, don't ask me about reliability. The first part of the answer is that the two photographs were taken from the direction of Radonjic Lake, which apparently is not a reliable part of the testimony because if you take it from Radonjic Lake, then of course it comes down to you and not as on the second photograph. So therefore, what Mr. Emmerson at this moment does is not to put the whole of the testimony, where there is some ambiguity, the last line also is not very clear to me, but at least there's one line which is abundantly clear: "This is what I saw with my own eyes when I was there." And Mr. Emmerson is now asking the witness, and he's fully entitled to do so, to see whether this is inconsistent with what this witness said. So either of the two must be -- perhaps still to be explained, but it's not -- you can't accept the two of it, which is: I arrived on the 11th. The photograph is what the witness -- what Dr. Dunjic saw with his own eyes when he was there. And this witness clearly testified on the 10th, perhaps also on the 9th, at least on the 10th with full explanation, these bodies were not there anymore. Then of course we have another puzzle. Has Dr. Dunjic been there on the 7th or what is the relation to April he mentions? That's all unclear. But this is an acceptable question to this witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, I'm not sure whether you have the question that I asked you in mind, but just to remind you. You've told us by reference to the photograph that we see at tab 2B that you can categorically state that those two bodies that we see in that photograph were no longer in the concrete section of the canal on the 10th when you attended. And I have just shown you a transcript from the evidence of Professor Dunjic, who did not attend the canal until the 11th and who, when shown that photograph, says in terms: "The second photograph is something I saw with my own eyes when I was on the location. We see two bodies next to the right-hand edge, depending on where you're looking from." Now, pausing there for a moment, I think you can agree, can you not, that the testimony given by Professor Dunjic in the Milutinovic case cannot be correct if what you've told the Trial Chamber about the position of those bodies on the 10th is right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't account for that. Anything I might say after this I believe there's nothing for me to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And would you agree --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a mismatch in the dates. The factual description is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, at the same time you are asking the witness something. He says: I do not know exactly when they arrived. You put to him the document in which it is recorded that he arrived on the 11th. So it's a matter of logic if it's true what the document says then even without the answer of the witness, there is contradiction. If not -- but this witness has earlier said that he had no direct contact with, so therefore let's leave it as it is. I mean, inconsistency and contradictions can be established not only through testimony but through logic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is, of course, one remaining hypothesis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which is the possibility that the bodies were moved again from the bottom section of the canal back up to the concrete section of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you have any reason to believe that the bodies were moved back up?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I really don't know what you want from me. Nobody had the reason to move corpses or to play with people or the corpses. I don't see how anybody would want to play with human lives. That's the least of anybody's desires. That's a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, whatever people may want to do or have good reasons to do, you say you have no reason whatsoever to believe that the corpses that you said were video-recorded in the concrete part of the canal on the 8th, that you said were not there anymore on the 10th. And you have got no reason whatsoever to -- to assume even that they were replaced there on the 11th. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it would. Yes. Madam Usher, could you already escort the witness out of the courtroom then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, same question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I need to confer with my colleagues before I can give you a reasonable answer at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you want to know what Mr. Emmerson is covering in the next 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, do you have already -- I'm not inviting you to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Without speculating, I think I've probably got about ten minutes, and again subject to further discussion with co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The impression of the Chamber was right that on Thursday the last session would not do. That was more or less accepted. Nevertheless, if three counsel together could see whether they could finish within one hour. Mr. Emmerson, if perhaps you negotiate with your colleagues who will put what questions, then we'll hear the result of such negotiations or compromises or agreements at 11.00, when we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, in response to the question the Chamber asked in terms of the time that I need, I, after consultation with my colleagues, feel that most efficacious and efficient use of time would be to cede ten minutes to Mr. Emmerson and I will not be asking any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would mean 45 minutes. The Chamber is inclined to have the next break at one minute to 12.00. Mr. Harvey, you're the third --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Not because I feel intimidated by that, but because I feel it's the most sensible use of all our time, I'm also going to yield my time to Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, do you think you could finish by one minute to 12.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, could you look at your witness statement again, please, this time page 16, paragraph 69, where you're commenting on a videotape of the recovery of remains at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the witness, Mr. Emmerson, it's page 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, page 22 of the Serbian original. Now, if you look at paragraph 69, letter d, and paragraph 69, letter i, please, first of all, just to remind yourself of what is written there. Now, is it correct then that one of the two individuals whose remains were discovered at Dashinoc was wearing a police shirt?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from 69(i), can you confirm that in that police shirt were found documents bearing the name Milka Radunovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you establish why it was that he was wearing a police shirt?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't establish why; however, at the time policemen used to give parts of their clothes to their relatives. They would give them shirts or vests.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know if, in fact, Milka Radunovic was a police officer or a reserve police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, to tab 1 and to the statement of Mr. Tomas at paragraph 54. In that statement Mr. Tomas is recorded as saying: "I recall" -- do you have that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 54. "I recall that Bajcetic found a personal ID and some other documents among those items, but I cannot remember the names that were mentioned on those documents. While we were at that location, a police unit, MUP, arrived and I remember that one of the police officers recognised one jacket that was found among the pieces of clothing as his father's. I do not know the name of this police officer. I knew that he was a police officer because he belonged to the police unit that had arrived. I don't know what the unit's task was. I simply saw them there." And then a little lower down he says this: "I do not know any further details in this respect because when the police officer recognised his missing father's jacket, I took Zenelj Alija away from the scene so that his presence would not cause any commotion." Now, pausing there. Do you remember a police officer arriving with a group of other officers who identified some of the clothing found there as belonging to his own father?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A group of police officers arrived. There was some ten of them or so, I believe that they were on the reserve strength, they came in a very small lorry. And objective was for them to secure the room where the on-site investigation was going on, and I don't really remember the detail of a policeman having recognised his father's shirt. Bogdan Tomas was maybe 30 or so metres away from us at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does the name Stanisa Radosevic mean anything to you in this context?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know of a man whose name is Slobodan Radosevic, whose documents were also there. I don't know anybody by the name of Stanisa Radosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard evidence in this trial from Stanisa Radosevic, who was the son of Slobodan Radosevic --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- describing that he attended the Dashinoc scene whilst there were investigators there examining the remains, and I just want to see if that in any way prompts your recollection of a relative of one of the deceased being present in police uniform.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not talk to that person at all. His name doesn't ring any bells. I am only familiar with the name of Slobodan Radosevic, whose documents were there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Were you aware that houses in Dashinoc had been set on fire by Serb forces immediately prior to your visit to Dashinoc?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see the village of Dashinoc at all whilst you were visiting the site?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came up to the two houses there. The people living there were rather poor. The houses were very modest, and at the time we were there they hadn't been torched. You had to go down a pathway, and on the left-hand side you came up to those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, can you confirm for the Tribunal, please, that it was the practice of the MUP and the PJP and the JSO to burn the houses of Albanians when they moved in to take control of a village?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besides being in Dasinovac and Rznic and on the lake, I did not go to any other villages at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That doesn't entirely answer my question. From your knowledge of being an RDB analyst in the area at the time and knowing of the clashes that were taking place, can you please tell the Tribunal: Was it the practice of the Serb forces to set fire to the houses of Albanians when they took control of a village?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this was the practice. I don't think that they had taken control over the villages. In none of the villages did the Serb forces take over control. They didn't control the area at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisa Radosevic, who attended the scene that you've described, has told us that the houses in the area had been burned down, but that's something you don't recall at all, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there, I suppose he resided there, and he would be more familiar with the area than I was. I was there only for one day, nothing else. I don't reside in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, you understand that the question I'm asking you is about the practice of Serb forces as a whole. Is it your testimony that you are not aware that Serb forces in that area around where you were based had a practice of putting houses to the torch when they moved into an Albanian village?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure why this is relevant for the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know whether this was --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the purposes of this witness. He's indicated several times he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he has evaded to answer the question, as a matter of fact. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, is it your evidence that you were not aware that it was the practice of Serb forces in the area where you were stationed at the time when they moved into an Albanian village to burn the houses and the crops and shoot the livestock?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very clear when I said that I don't know whether that was the practice. There may have been such cases, that's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
