utterances.text: Let's not focus on the semantic issue of what is practice and what is not practice. Are you aware of Serb forces burning houses and crops, whether that happened if they were in Albanian villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say exactly. I know as I was passing by on the Djakovica-Decani-Pec road that I also saw some houses smoldering. Now, as to what village that was, who had burnt the houses down, it's very difficult for me to say that, I really can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you personally observed. In the -- in your position did you ever receive information about such things that had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received information that certain villages, i.e., certain houses had been torched. But pursuant to this information, one couldn't really conclude that that was common practice and that all the houses were torched when a village was entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said you could not conclude that this was common practice, but that information was about houses and crops torched by Serbian forces; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard about houses that were torched. I don't know about the crops, but I repeat nobody ever told me that this was practice, that this was customarily done when a village was entered. I never received information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And when you say, "when a village was entered," you mean to say when a village was entered by Serb forces. I leave alone what kind of forces exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Serb forces which were part of an armed conflict or which were engaged in an operation or in an action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did anybody ever give you a justification for why it was considered legitimate to burn civilians' houses?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to move to another topic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, in your question suddenly the houses become civilian houses, which is as far as I understand not the testimony of the witness so therefore -- but in view of the answer I think we can proceed. But I would just like you not to hide these few elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If it needs to be clarified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, in view of the answer of the witness there's no need. It's just for future occasions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 65 of your witness statement, Mr. Bajcetic, you refer in the last sentence of that paragraph to the recovery of a 30-year-old male in a drain area, a concrete sewer, adjacent to the economic farm. This is your own witness statement, Mr. Bajcetic, which is tab 14.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, if you can bear with me, please. 14 -- oh, it's in the other binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the end of paragraph 65 you refer to the recovery, inside a concrete sewer adjacent to the economic farm, of a body of a man of approximately 30 years old.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you recall that body being removed from the concrete sewer yourself, were you present?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I personally saw that and one of these men was removing the concrete grid. The body was revealed. It was a 30-year-old man in a jacket. The body was then taken out of the place where it was positioned, but I did not stay up to the end. I did not attend that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm going to put some passages from some statements to you in connection with that body. Once I've done that I want to ask you one or two questions about them but I'm going to put them to you first. For your information that body was given a label of RE1 and was subsequently, some time later, identified by DNA analysis as a man called Mehmet Rrustemaj. If you would take the brown volume for a moment and first of all, look at tab 7. There's just one line in that statement I want to draw to your attention. In paragraph 11 -- this is a statement made by the wife of Mehmet Rrustemaj. And as you will see in the first line of paragraph 11, she records that her husband was last seen alive at her home by her at 11.00 in the morning on the 30th of August. If you would now turn, please, to tab 10 there is a further statement from that lady, and on this I'm afraid you're going to have to rely on a translation from the interpreters in the English and I'm going to read to you a passage from the bottom of page 2 and top of page 3 of that statement. She says this: "Whilst my husband was alive he was always under pressure from the Serbian police. He was beaten and tortured many times. He was accused of keeping weapons, but in general it was well known that my husband did not like Serbs. In particular -- in particular he had problems with officers known as Rade and Milutin, they often used to beat my husband in Gjakove police station where they both worked. Rade was a small man and Milutin was small [sic], they both spoke perfect Albanian although they were Serbs. My husband suffered with problems in his knees due to one of the last beatings that he suffered at the hands of these officers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you misspoke when you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that Milutin was small as well. He was tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, "Milutin was tall". I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: She continues: "One of the other reasons my husband had problems with these people is that my parents are from the village of Prekaz. My father is from the Jashari family (who were killed by Serbian forces in 1998). My father was a second or third cousin of Adem Jashari. Our family connection meant that the Serbian police always suspected Mehmet of involvement with weapons. Everyone in this area knew of our family connection." Just pausing there for a moment, there's one further passage I want to put to you before I put a series of questions to you. If you turn behind tab 11 this is a statement from a man called Islam Rruci, who was an acquaintance of the individual whose remains were recovered in that sewer, Mehmet Rrustemaj. And on page 2 of his witness statement he says this: "I do not think that Mehmet had any problems with anyone apart from the man named Rade who I know he was afraid of. I know that Mehmet's house was often visited by Serbs. I'm not 100 per cent sure of the reason, but I believe he was in dispute with the Serb Rade Vlahovic from the village and he was afraid that this Serb might seek revenge against his family. He was always having problems with Rade who was a civilian police officer from Gjakove. They had argued over the market spot that Mehmet sold honey from. I think Rade wanted the spot for a friend of his." Pausing there. First of all, you've told us that you know Rade Vlahovic as an officer stationed at Gjakove police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there more than one Rade Vlahovic at Gjakove police station, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was he a civilian police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you describe him for us, please?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have been around 170 centimetres tall, brownish hair, medium build. I don't believe I would recognise him even now if I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Are you able to shed any light on the suggestion that one of the individuals whose remains were recovered during the investigation had had prior problems with Rade Vlahovic from Gjakove police station?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll turn to another topic then, if I may, please. You have described in your witness statement the fact that bullet casings were collected from the area around the canal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think some significance was attached to the fact that these were bullet casings of Chinese manufacture; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just explain to us what the significance of the fact that they were of Chinese manufacture.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the ammunition was used, that type of ammunition, apparently the sound the ammunition made when fired was different from the sound produced by the Serbian-made ammunition. I believe the difference was in the charge itself and that they generally referred to that sort of ammunition as crackers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So was Chinese ammunition associated with the KLA or with the Serb forces or with both?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was associated with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did the Serb forces use Chinese ammunition?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, to my knowledge they did not. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I just want to see if you can help us for a moment, please. If you could just look in the brown file behind tab 4 for a moment. Now, if you look in the first few lines of this document, you can see the heading I think in the middle of the page: "Ambush plan." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look above it, please --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- does it record there an agreement between members of the Secretariat of the Interior in Gjakove and members of the department of state security in Peje and Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This would be an agreement then between the SUP and the department that you worked for; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here. We had never had such an agreement in Djakovica, I'm sure about that -- at least I did not attend a single meeting where such an agreement was reached. Whether something along those lines happened, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the answer to that may lie in the date, because if you look under the words "ambush plan," the first numbered paragraph refers to an ambush that is to take place in January 1999, and I think by then you had left, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. It has nothing to do with my stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. You had left by then. Mr. Tomas, on the other hand, was still there, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you can see in the lines at the top that the plan is directed at information that terrorists located in Jablanica and Bucane will be moving long the Kosuric-Glodjane-Nepolje road at a particular time; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just questioning the relevance --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- if -- given the date that was referred to by my friend, I'm not sure what the relevance is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's apparent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the relevance comes clear from the previous questions and from testimony the Chamber already heard on this matter before. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you now look to the paragraph with Roman numeral V. In the second sentence of that paragraph does it indicate that: "The platoon leader of the PJP is to provide grenade launchers and ammunition manufactured in China ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at VIII, Roman numeral VIII, does it record that in addition to camouflage uniforms, boots, bullet-proof vests, and so forth, members of the PJP should be equipped with long-barrelled weapons with two combat ammunition sets, while each squad should have one hand-held launcher and 30 bullets manufactured in China; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you think of any legitimate reason why the department that you had been working for, state security, should enter into an agreement with the PJP to issue members of the PJP not only with regular combat ammunition sets, but in addition with 30 bullets manufactured in China?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, really. This is the first time I hear of these facts, that's number one. And number two, I wasn't there in that time-period. Presumably, this agreement was reached under circumstances that were quite different from those when I was there. I cannot say anything else about a period of time when I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand you can't comment on the plan that was reached, although as you've told us a moment ago it was reached at a time when your colleague Mr. Tomas was still serving in Gjakove. I understand that you're not in a position to comment on the content of the plan. The question I'm asking you is: Can you conceive of any legitimate reason why it would be necessary in addition to regular ammunition to ensure that the members of the PJP were carrying rounds of ammunition which are associated with use by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, that question has been put to the witness and he has answered. And he said, "I don't know, really." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn behind tab 5 for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I should have slowed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd like you to look, please, at paragraph 160 of that document which is an excerpt from the Prosecution's pre-trial brief in the Milutinovic case. I think if you look at the allegation there made: "Other concealment attempts were made in advance of the killings. For example, in one MUP order of January 1999 troops were assigned to ambush suspected KLA members and were ordered to use Chinese ammunition. Chinese ammunition was habitually used by the KLA but not by the forces of the FRY and Serbia. This deliberate attempt to frame the KLA for killing Albanians played into later propaganda attempts by members of the joint criminal enterprise to blame civilian casualties on KLA in-fighting." Mr. Bajcetic, was there a policy within RDB Gjakove of which you were aware to seek to implicate the KLA for crimes committed by or at the instigation of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was down there, I assert that this wasn't the case. These matters that you have just read out from paragraph 160 are completely new to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, you said a little while ago in answer to a question concerning the canal that the idea of the movement of bodies was, as I understand it in your testimony, one that you wholly rejected as a possibility, the idea that the bodies were moved and manipulated by the Serb authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about any such thing for -- that's for sure, if anything of the sort existed, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Would you turn to paragraph 153 in that excerpt that I've just given you. This is a reference in the first line to Vlastimir Djordjevic, a man who, according to the statement I showed you at tab 13, attended on the 8th with Mr. Tomas. And the allegation made by the Prosecution in relation to Mr. Djordjevic is that he coordinated the clearing up of bodies in seeking --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is entirely irrelevant to the matter we're dealing with in this particular case. He's obviously dealing with -- he's obviously raising issues that relate to a different case entirely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Emmerson wants to hear from this witness whether he is aware to what extent we are talking about here about incidents and whether it was anything more, and he's entitled to do so. At the same time, Mr. Emmerson, I don't remember that the witness said that there was no possibility that they would have done it. I think, as a matter of fact, the witness said that he could not understand one reason why one would do such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not about possibilities. So to that extent I think you misrepresented --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to know how much of this you are aware of. I'll read it again. "Djordjevic coordinated, pursuant to Stojiljkovic's orders, the 'clearing-up' of bodies in secret mass graves at several locations in Serbia. Bodies were driven by MUP officers to one of several locations in Serbia, including Lake Perucac, Bajina Basta, and the SAJ's own firing range at Batajnica, near Belgrade. At Batajnica the bodies were placed by MUP officers in a mass grave on the firing range itself. The entire operation was conducted in secret. "Djordjevic was personally involved in the operation. He spoke via telephone and in person with low-level MUP officers regarding the details of burial and his own driver was involved in driving some of the trucks. Djordjevic said to a MUP officer that the burial would be part of 'mopping-up' in Kosovo, a 'number one' secret. Several of these mass graves were exhumed by authorities in Serbia beginning in 2001. Over 900 bodies have been exhumed thus far. Autopsies and DNA evidence, coupled with the discovery of identity cards and other personal effects with the bodies, will prove that the bodies belonged to persons killed in Kosovo during the indictment period, including individuals whose names appear on schedules to the indictment." Now, Mr. Bajcetic, can I be clear, when you gave the testimony a little while ago about being unable to conceive of reasons why bodies might be moved around, were you unaware of these allegations against Vlastimir Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state that I absolutely did not know about this information. I heard them over the media, but I do believe that they are -- that they make no sense, in other words, but that's now up to this case to determine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You are aware, Mr. Bajcetic, that large numbers of remains of Kosovar Albanians were dug-up at a grave at Batajnica in 2001 and are still being repatriated to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It was publicised by the media. I did not know about that until the media started reporting on that and until Vlastimir Djordjevic was referred to as the person involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know from the document that you've seen in cross-examination today that a senior member of the SUP in the building where you worked has recorded that very gentleman of attending this crime scene of the so-called reconnaissance on the 8th of September, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, but I've already said that I was not aware of that at the time and that I was in no way able to have any influence over who was to compose that reconnaissance group.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it still your evidence that you cannot conceive of any reason or, indeed, any possibility of remains being moved by Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, what the witness said: "Nobody had the reason to move corpses or to play with people or the corpses. I don't see how anybody would want to play with human lives."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "That's the least of anybody's desires."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now to say whether the witness could conceive or not. I mean, is his imagination at this time --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- worth to take part of your remaining 14 minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've heard the passage the Judge just read to you. Does that remain your evidence, Mr. Bajcetic? I'm sorry, I don't think we're receiving translation. Could you speak into the microphone, please. Does that remain your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I turn finally to one other topic from your witness statement, paragraphs 67 and 68. You refer there to the finding of further human remains towards the end of September near the economic farm, but you say that you were not present when those remains were discovered or exhumed but you know that the same RDB colleague --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you know that the same RDB colleague who made the above-mentioned recordings was present when these remains were discovered but you did not know whether he made any video-recordings on that occasion. Just for the sake of --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, can we be absolutely clear. Can you give us the name of the individual you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the cameraman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, could you give us his name, please.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether his name should be mentioned or not. I'm not sure if he should be called before the Tribunal. His name is contained in the documents, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy for the witness to give that testimony in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we turn into private session so that the outside world will not know your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two questions, if I may, on this topic. Could you turn to tab 6, please, in the brown file. This document purports to be a record of an on-site investigation conducted on the 23rd of September by an investigating judge called Kemal Cindrak in relation to remains found at the economic farm. And I just wanted to ask you about one aspect of it. In the second main paragraph the report records that: "The scene," that is to say the scene of this alleged finding, "was secured by," two employees of Djakovica SUP. One of whom is named by Predrag Stojanovic. First of all, Predrag Stojanovic, were you aware that he was a member of the family whose premises was used to launch the 24th attack on the Haradinaj compound?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know or did you know Predrag Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him on several occasions. I believe he is a tall skinny person. I didn't know him that well. I didn't know most of the people in SUP for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. He was based at Gjakove, though?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him. He was driving a lorry. This was his private business or something. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know if he was a member of the PJP at any time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. One final topic then. Paragraph 62 of your witness statement, you refer to a term --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which statement, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 62 of your own witness statement, which is tab 14 of the yellow binder. You say there in relation to your time at the canal: "I also remember there was a turned-over vehicle with the bodies of a missing young married Catholic Albanian couple." And you say at paragraph 63: "The turned-over vehicle was situated in the middle of the above-mentioned basin, which was about 4 to 5 metres beneath the concrete cascade." Can you tell us, please, what you can remember about those bodies.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This car was below the concrete cascade. It's a larger area like sort of a small lake. This was a car, and I can't recall the colour, and the people who went down there recovered two bodies of a man and a woman. They said at the time that this was a married couple, Catholic Albanians, from the village of Skivjan between Djakovica and Decani. I don't have any other information about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see where the bodies were recovered from, specifically?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not observe as they pulled the bodies out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this: Were you given any information at the time as to where the bodies were recovered from specifically?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was only said that two Albanians from the village of Skivjani, were missing and that the two bodies in the car were theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I then take it that you have no further questions and that the same would be true for Mr. Harvey. Then, Ms. Issa, we have to stop at one minute to 12.00 anyhow, so I don't think it makes any sense to -- now to start re-examination, if there's any need to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, there will be some re-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will have a break. At 12.00 there is a swearing-in ceremony at this Tribunal where the Judges will attend. That means that most likely we will resume at 20 minutes past 12.00, but it could be a bit later depending on how much time the swearing-in ceremony will take. We stand adjourned until the end of that ceremony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, before I give you an opportunity to re-examine the witness, I'd like to inquire with you whether you have any difficulties in doing that where we have not yet received from the Prosecution -- from the Defence an indication as to what documents they've used they intend to tender. It might be that it doesn't cause you any problem at this moment, and in that case I would invite Defence counsel to notify the Chamber as soon as possible what are the documents tendered. But if you say I've got problems with it now, I'll then give that priority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps out of an abundance of caution, Your Honour, we might just do it now. If -- if it doesn't take too much time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Abundance of caution -- if you need it. If you say: I don't know how to re-examine the witness if I don't know, then we'll do it now. If you say: No, I'm confident that I can re-examine the witness and deal with it then, then Mr. Emmerson has -- and Mr. Guy-Smith and Mr. Harvey have a bit more time to prepare.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, I can proceed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bajcetic.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, the last session you were asked a series of questions regarding allegations that bodies were moved to or dumped in the Lake Radonjic canal. Are you aware of any bodies having been moved to or been dumped in the Lake Radonjic canal area by Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to call-up Exhibit P379, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps while we're waiting for that. On Thursday, Mr. Bajcetic, you were asked a number of questions about clashes taking place in the Lake Radonjic canal area. And what I'd like you to do is to have a look at the map that is on your screen at the moment, that's the same map that you've marked during your examination-in-chief --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- where you've indicated that this area was inaccessible to Serbian forces without staging an operation. Could you orient yourself on that map, perhaps take a moment, and just specifically indicate where the clashes took place in the Lake Radonjic canal area.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often the clashes were taking place in Nadeloc [as interpreted], Dubrava, Glodjane, Ratis, Rznic, Dasinovac area. This is the part where the clashes took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether or not any clashes took place in the specific area where the bodies were ultimately found?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were clashes in that area as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who did these clashes involve, between whom?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The participants in the clashes were members of the KLA and the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The SUP or the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all intents and purposes, this is the same thing. The secretariat is somewhat a lower unit at the level of a municipality, otherwise the MUP and the SUP are practically the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And on those occasions when you say there were clashes in this area, can you indicate how long these clashes lasted?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the -- how long they lasted, for example, a day, or what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's exactly what I mean. How long would a clash last?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hours in the course of one day, maybe three or four hours in the course of one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And after the clashes or particular clash would -- would be over, what -- who had control of the area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SUP would then withdraw because there were no conditions set in place for the check-points to be set-up and the area would be regained by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you indicate when the clashes took place, specifically in the Lake Radonjic canal area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically it happened in the cases when members of the KLA attacked either a police patrol or a police check-point or information would be received that civilians in the area were threatened. This would result in a conflict. It was not possible to locate the perpetrators of such attacks or issuers of such threats without an open conflict or an action, an engagement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And during what time-period did this occur?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was down there between the 1st of July and the end of my stay there, these clashes were a continuing occurrence. Sometimes they were of lower intensity, sometimes of higher intensity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You mentioned, sir, that these clashes occurred when there was a -- an attack on a police check-point. Can you indicate where the -- where these check-points were that were attacked to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, if that's intended to focus the witness on part of his answer, then I have no objection, but his answer went much broader than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I am focusing on part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you look at the map, sir, and orient yourself and answer that question. I can ask it again if you need me to.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the clashes were in the Babaloc-Rastavica area around Prilep, Crnobreg [Realtime transcript read in error "Crnibreg"], mostly in that part, and I can't see Streoc here, Donji Streoc as well. That's where the clashes happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, what I'm going to ask you to do at this stage is if I can call-up Exhibit D32. And while we're waiting for that, can you -- can you explain why it is that the Serbian forces had to retreat after such clashes took place?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a simple reason. It was not possible to secure any logistical support in the area. The KLA were in their own part of the field there. That was their turf.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you say "that was their turf," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that the Albanian population prevailed there and the KLA could count logistical support in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was it ever possible during that period of time between July 1998 until the end of your time there -- or at least until the end of September 1998 for the Serbian forces to maintain control over the area after such a clash?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think "maintain control" requires specificity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think the witness understood my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- let me just re-read the question. Yes. Ms. Issa, on the basis of the evidence the Chamber has heard, perhaps it's good to be more specific because the time-period covered is July until the end of September, where we know that -- at least the testimony until now has made clear to us that the situation has changed considerably, whether you're talking about early August, early September, et cetera. So therefore, you're invited to get a more specific answer to the extent the witness is able to give it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Mr. Bajcetic, after the Serbian forces engaged in a clash or one may refer to something as combat with the KLA, was it possible for the Serbian forces to take control over the villages that you mentioned or the Lake Radonjic canal area during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I think the question as posed calls for speculation and also outside of this witness's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- outside of this witness's knowledge and level of expertise because, once again, the question of what "maintain control" means becomes the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get -- you have described, Mr. Bajcetic, to us that there were clashes, and since the conditions were not there to have check-points there. Was there at any time when you were there, was there a situation where the Serb forces did not withdraw immediately after such clashes but were able to, partly or wholly, be in control of villages or areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, not for a single moment did the Serb forces control that area, save for the short period of time when they were investigating the victims on the lake. They never had any other form of control over those villages nor were they ever stationed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was that limited to the very small area, that is, where the canal is, or was it a wider area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was limited to that area, i.e., the road between the Djakovica-Decani road and that area between that road and the Radonjic Lake was secured, and this lasted for the duration of the investigation and the exhumation of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what do you consider the period of the investigation? Is that to start on the 8th of any -- of September or any earlier and lasting until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, this lasted for no more than ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to clarify your last answer, Mr. Bajcetic, when you say this lasted for no more than ten days, which ten days are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period from the 8th, from the moment when the bodies were discovered at Radonjic Lake, to the moment when the other group of bodies were found in the Ekonomija sector, and the latter is where I did not attend the event. Some bodies were found there, some people were buried there, and after that we no longer had access to the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why is it that after that you had no longer access to the area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit could not stay there without any logistical support. The KLA army was on their turf there. Their houses were there. There were people there who could provide them with all sorts of support.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you look at your screen you'll see a map, Mr. Bajcetic. I'd like to ask you to first orient yourself to this map and to think about where precisely these clashes took place between July 1st, 1998, until the end of September. And with the assistance of Madam Usher I will ask you, once you've oriented yourself, to draw a -- or mark an X on the villages where the clashes took place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just concerned at page 68, line 18, through to -- I'm sorry, page 66, line 18, through to line 23 the witness has given his testimony in word form. I'm not concerned as to whether or not it be placed on the map. If it is to be placed on the map, then the answers that he's given from page 66, line 18, through to and including line 23, ought to be in his mind and marked on the map as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're mixing up -- now you're talking about page 66, which apparently is a mistake, I take it you're referring to page 68, as you did before. I read in the transcript there: "Most of the clashes were in the Babaloc-Rastavica area around Prilep," it says Crnibreg, but it might be Crnobreg, "mostly in that part but I can't see Streoc there, Donji Streoc as well. That's where the clashes happened."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact I was referring to 66, 18: "Most of the clashes were taking place in Streoc, Dubrava," I think there is a spelling error -- "Streoc, Dubrava, Glodjane, Ratis, Rznic," and the arrow I think was Dashinoc area. "This is the part where the clashes took place. "Are you aware of whether or not any clashes took place in the specific area where the bodies were ultimately found? "There were clashes in that area as well."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Issa, is your exercise now to have that all marked on the map because the Chamber now having heard this case for many, many months could by heart take you to the villages on the map the witness was referring to, apart from Streoc which didn't appear on the map. So if that's the purpose of the exercise, I think we can do without. If there's any further purpose, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The only purpose was to clarify where the clashes were which Mr. Bajcetic refers to but if Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We know where the villages are --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, on Thursday, in your testimony, for the Chamber's reference at page 6447 of the transcript, you mentioned that Rade Vlahovic could not reach the home of his parents, that's at lines 23 through 25. My first question is: Where did Rade Vlahovic's parents live?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in Dasinovac as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why is it that he could not reach the home of his parents, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he would have been captured by KLA, and I can only assume what would have transpired in that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how is it that you know this?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time, nobody moved, none -- no civilian Serbs moved in the area, and especially not those who were working for the SUP at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you say "at that time," can you be more specific as to what time you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the time when I was there, between the 1st of July and the 30th of October -- or the 30th of September, I can't be sure of the date. During that period of time, no civilians moved around freely, and especially not somebody who worked in the SUP. He -- such a person would not have stood a chance if they had gone to that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Referring you then to a copy of -- I don't know if you have a copy of your statement in front of you, but referring you to paragraph 37 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the yellow binder under number 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Paragraph --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Number 14 in the binder. You say midway through that paragraph,

utterances.speaker: MR. BAJCETIC
utterances.text: "These two MUP officers could obtain such information because they had close ties with local Albanians who did not approve or did not support the KLA policy or the KLA activities. The family members of these two MUP officers had refused to leave their homes despite all kinds of pressure and harassment exerted by the KLA, but because the KLA check-points -- because of the KLA check-points, these people could not leave their villages anymore and they became disconnected from their relatives because they could no longer travel and there was no means of communication." Now, when you say "these people could not leave their villages anymore," during what time-period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period between the 1st of July and the end of my stay, for as long as I stayed. As I just told you, they could not use the roads, they could not reach Pec, Decani, or Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You also refer to a second officer in your statement, Momcilo Stijovic, and on Thursday at page 6413, for the Chamber's reference lines 22 to 25 of the transcript, you say that: "Momcilo Stijovic was helped by the Albanians to transport some of his belongings out of his house by tractor. This was part of his effort to evacuate his belongings." Could you explain why Momcilo Stijovic had to evacuate his belongings.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the simple reason that he was unable to live there any longer. After the pressure exerted on him, his life would have been hell. Most likely he would have been killed, murdered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to clarify that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to -- I'm going to object to the speculation made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can't object against an answer, Mr. -- You can later tell us that it was speculation, but Ms. Issa did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take your point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- call for such a speculation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How is it that you learned Momcilo Stijovic had to leave because he was -- he had -- as you put it, his life was made hell?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Momcilo Stijovic told us that personally, that some Albanians had helped him to have some of his belongings transported to Djakovica. He told that to us in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, who exerted this pressure on Momcilo Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanians or, specifically, the KLA. They exerted pressure on all the Serb families present in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Exerted pressure on them to do what?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To move out of the area, not only him but all of them, including of course Momcilo Stijovic himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, these are rather general statements. If you could lay a further factual foundation, then it certainly would assist the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How is it that you -- that you know, Mr. Bajcetic, that there was pressure on all the Serbs to move -- to leave the area caused by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite clear to me that whoever was not in the area finds it hard to understand. The entire Albanian population, among whom the KLA was active as an organisation or a paramilitary organisation, wanted to have the Serbs leave the area. That was the sort of pressure that was exerted. The corpses found at Lake Radonjic served to show that it was impossible for them to stay there because their life was in danger -- their lives were in danger, and that's the essence of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But more specifically, Mr. Bajcetic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Emmerson would like to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would, if I may. First of all, I'm at a loss to understand how this type of general evidence arises out of cross-examination. And secondly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- however the questions are put, the whole thrust of the questions and answers and the interchange between counsel and the witness is designed to elicit generalisation when the Trial Chamber has heard specific evidence about specific time-periods. Had this material been part of cross-examination, then the situation may have been different, but in order to put it in its proper context - and I'm obviously seeking to avoid the necessity to ask the Chamber for leave to further cross-examine - but we've had quite a considerable amount of evidence about Serb families voluntarily leaving the area in April, in anticipation of what was perceived to be a situation in which the Albanian population was arming itself, and to at this stage in this way invite this line of -- it's not an objection to the form of a question, it's an objection to an entire line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, two issues. The first one, how does it result -- how does the need to put these questions result from cross-examination, that's the first one; and the second one is: Why rely on general -- a general description rather than to rely on the rather precise evidence the Chamber received earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, firstly, Your Honour, as when I began this line of questioning I specifically referred to page 6413 of the transcript of 28 June 2007, and my -- the questions arise specifically from the question that was initially put by Mr. Emmerson to the witness which related to Momcilo Stijovic and Rade Vlahovic. At line 21, Mr. Emmerson asked the

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The witness responded: "To put it simply, I base it on the fact that at the time I heard from Momcilo Stijovic himself that Albanians had helped him to transport some of his belongings and essentially evacuate from the area." So I was trying to perhaps get more specific evidence in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the second matter is about the general character of the -- of the evidence. If you want to put questions to the witness in respect of this, whenever he starts saying what happened in the whole of the area with everyone, would you then please take him back to more specifics. For example, you asked him, upon my urging you to do so, how he knew, and then Mr. -- then you continued, Mr. Bajcetic, to describe the situation, whereas the question of Ms. Issa was another one, that was: How did you get knowledge of that? How could you make statements on what happened with everyone? What was the source of your knowledge? And you then continued to describe what happened to everyone rather than to tell us what the source of your knowledge was. Could you please then return to the last question -- I see that there are two Defence counsel on their feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have nothing further to say about the second objection. Your Honour has taken the point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and I hope it will be heeded. As regards the first, and the passage that Ms. Issa has refers to, may I make it absolutely what the position of the Defence is: I cross-examined this witness, page 6413, as to whether the information allegedly provided by the two detainees Alija and Musaj was confirmatory information to that which had previously been provided by Rade Vlahovic and Momcilo Stijovic. And I asked the witness who they were and he explained who they were and continued -- this is line 18: "My impression is that both of them had been on friendly terms from some Albanians from the area before the conflict and during the conflict. "What do you base that impression on?" And the witness gave some information about transportation of belongings. To say that a line of questioning which involves general evidence about the movements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think, Mr. Emmerson, may I interrupt you here. A general line of questioning, I do agree. Some further specifics on matters that were dealt with and where there's a sufficient link is another matter. So if we get rid of the general line of the questioning and limit ourselves at this moment to more specific questions, then Ms. Issa may proceed. Mr. Guy-Smith, you were on -- you're not anymore. I take it that is a sign that Ms. Issa can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am somewhat worried because as I am reading the transcript it seems as if it was Ms. Issa who was posing the question on page 6413. Perhaps I'm mistaken. I've been back and forth on the transcript a couple of times, at 6413.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Emmerson who -- no, let me -- no --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact Mr. Guy-Smith is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see on page 6412, Ms. Issa and then the questions come and it's not Mr. Emmerson. That makes, by the way, the matter even more problematic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now granted Ms. Issa an opportunity to put some additional questions. Ms. Issa, it -- when you are referring to those lines, you at least created the suggestion that those were questions put in cross-examination; they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That was my mistake, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Since I granted something, I'm not taking it back from you at this very moment, but would you please limit yourself very much to one or two more specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will. Perhaps I'll just move on to a different area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Earlier today, Mr. Bajcetic, you were referred to paragraph 61 of your statement and then you were referred to paragraph 62, and you were asked some questions regarding the bodies or as to information that you received about the missing young married Catholic Albanian couple. Just to clarify, can you indicate who gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot pin-point the name of the person who provided the information; however, when I was describing the way we came by information, I explained that bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you receive this information?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was in early September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. Bajcetic, that you mentioned at one stage that you had not been to the Lake Radonjic canal area before 10th September 1998, and my question is: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Sreten Camovic's decision. He decided who was to go where and when. He told me that I should go on the 10th, and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But before that -- before you found out about the bodies that were -- that were located at the Lake Radonjic canal, had you been there? Had you been to that area specifically?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it wasn't safe at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why was it not safe?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't safe due to the presence of armed members of the KLA in the area. They held the territory. It's not just I that -- who wasn't safe. It wasn't safe for anyone to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware of whether any other members of the RDB going there before September 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any need for further questions, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Short of registering my concern about the line of questioning which was interrupted and which Ms. Issa abandoned, I don't propose to seek the Trial Chamber's permission to further cross-examine the witness in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey? Mr. Bajcetic, this then concludes your testimony in this court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to thank you very much for having answered --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the questions. I know it's quite far away from your home, I'm also aware that you had to stay over the weekend which you didn't like that very much. It's appreciated that you stayed and returned on this Monday. I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, would you escort Mr. Bajcetic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, are you now able to give us the documents -- the numbers of the documents you would like to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but may I give -- may I give Your Honours the numbers immediately after court rises. I intended to tender those documents used in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then that's the starting point, then you provide Madam Registrar with a list --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of those documents. I take it, Ms. Issa, then the Prosecution is sufficiently informed for the time being. We'll formalise the matters then once we've received that list. Then for the next witness I think we have a couple of procedural issues, that is, protective measures; that is exclusion of certain areas of the evidence as we find it in that 92 ter statement; and then third, the redaction of the 92 ter statement or at least a response to the suggestions made by the Prosecution to take out certain portions of the statement to say it very briefly, that is the portions suggested in an e-mail of the 28th of June by Mr. Dixon to, I would say, all relevant persons relating to paragraphs 11, 13, 20, 32, 33, 55, 96, 98, 100, 170, 171, and then as far as ballistics are concerned we are talking about paragraphs 184, and 186 up to and including 190.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is one addition. We sent an e-mail --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- apparently it was not also sent to the Chambers as I've seen here. The only addition to those mentioned by the Chamber would be paragraph 97, the second sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Is there any -- have the parties discussed, Mr. Dutertre, a possible redaction of the statement so that there will be no further objection against admission of a 92 ter statement into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I received the objections raised by the Defence teams in advance, and I want to thank my colleagues. But unfortunately I wasn't able on Friday to meet with them because I was unwell to tell them the position of the Prosecution, to tell the Prosecution's position, concerning each of these objections. I can do so now, if you so wish, going through paragraph by paragraph, following the suggestions made by the Defence. I apologise for this delay, which is due to something totally unforeseen and irresistible, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether that's the most practical way of proceeding. We also could move to one of the other matters, that is, for example, protective measures, and then see whether the parties can resolve some of the problems. For -- just give one example. If I'm looking at paragraph 13, I think, as a matter of fact, Mr. Dutertre, that if you would change the first line in the following way, to start 13 with: "The last remaining Serbs were expelled or kidnapped from Decani and the area on both sides of the Djakovica-Decani-Pec road," then the issue of the armed conflict as a legal concept is taken out. At the same time, the factual basis for it, "KLA bunkers and trenches were set-up off that road but almost ... " would still be there, also including the last line: "The KLA were firing at both civilian and police vehicles." At least I get the impression that that would meet at least the concern expressed that the first sentence of paragraph 13 is an expression of opinion on a question of law for the Trial Chamber. So I can imagine that sitting together and trying to resolve these matters would be more efficient because we have quite a number of them. It would take us at least the next half an hour, whereas the Chamber would perhaps prefer to have this done outside the court. And the Chamber accepts that there were good reasons not to do so until now, but half an hour left, perhaps we could spend that in a better way. It would also allow the Chamber to receive a new copy of the 92 ter statement with redactions. Therefore, I would, as a matter of fact, prefer to go into closed session and to deal with the protective measures. As far as the ballistic evidence is concerned, the Chamber received this very morning I think one hour ago, the response by the Prosecution. And perhaps it's better that we take our time this afternoon to see what our conclusion should be on the basis of the request filed by the Defence and the response given by the Prosecution. So I therefore suggest that we first go into closed session and -- or would private session -- let me just -- whether we can go into private session or not depends on the protective measures asked. I think they were quite limited. There were just - and therefore we would have to move into closed session - was face and voice distortion only. If that's the case, we have to turn into closed session first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I got French on the English channel, which is always pleasant for my ears but ... Yes. After the witness will start his -- the substance of his testimony tomorrow, I do understand that the next two witnesses most likely will be first Aleksandric and then Dr. Dunjic, but there is one uncertainty about a witness to appear who has been subpoenaed, where we are not fully sure on what will happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I indicated to the Legal Officer on Friday that given the nature of that witness's testimony, were he to appear in response to the subpoena, he is not a witness in respect of whom it would be convenient for his testimony to be taken in my absence on Thursday. May I place that formally on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is now on the record. At the same time, there are so many uncertainties about the present situation that we can't resolve that now at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, you have put your concerns on the record. If there is no other matter at this moment to be raised, then we'll adjourn until tomorrow the -- at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: witness:  "What do you base that impression on?"
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
